answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove fraud. Creating a hollow shell identity then costs real capital, not just a new keypair, so an attacker must risk funds for every fake agent. Honest agents earn fees over time and rise toward the zenith of a reputation ranking, while a single umber flag, a verified complaint, freezes payouts until the dispute clears. Sybils therefore scale in cost, not in number.
